rule: Every label in the dashboard uses the full official name. The short form appears only here, beside its full name, so a reader can match it to a state document.

terms.plain: The part of the Minnesota Department of Human Services that runs programs for older adults and people with disabilities.
terms.source: ADSA Equity and Inclusion Implementation Plan

terms.plain: The division inside the Aging and Disability Services Administration that runs disability waiver programs.
The state agency.
Services a person is likely to need on an ongoing basis. They can be given at home and in the community, or in a facility.

Services given in a person's own home, residence or community, not in a facility. Includes the Brain Injury, Community Alternative Care, Community Access for Disability Inclusion, Developmental Disabilities, Elderly Waiver and Alternative Care programs, plus state home care.
Home and community-based services for a person with a brain injury who would otherwise need care in a facility.
Home and community-based services for a person who would otherwise need hospital-level care.

terms.full: Community Access for Disability Inclusion Waiver
terms.plain: Home and community-based services for a person with a disability who would otherwise need nursing-facility care.
Home and community-based services for a person with a developmental disability.
Home and community-based services for a person age 65 or older who would otherwise need nursing-home care.
Home and community-based services for Minnesotans 65 or older who need nursing-home level care but are not yet financially eligible for Medical Assistance.
The county that pays for a person's services.
Runs July 1 to June 30. State fiscal year 2022 is July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2022.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Same as state fiscal year: July 1 to June 30.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Engage phase, waiver service. Helps a person decide whether they want to work.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Waiver service. Used only in fiscal year 2022; after that it split into a Plan phase and a Find phase.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Plan phase, waiver service. Helps a person plan for work and set work goals. Used since fiscal year 2023.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Find phase, waiver service. Helps a person find a job. Meant to be used only when Vocational Rehabilitation Services or State Services for the Blind is unavailable.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Find phase. Helps a person find a job. Not a waiver service; the usual choice in the Find phase.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Find phase. Helps a person find a job. Like Vocational Rehabilitation Services, but for people who are blind, have low vision, or are deafblind.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Short for Vocational Rehabilitation Services and State Services for the Blind together.
Keep phase, waiver service. Helps a person keep a job, one-to-one with a job coach.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Keep phase, waiver service. A job coach supports several people at once who all work the same job. The state's own note: this service often leads to segregation.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: Waiver service. Helps a person build work skills. Usually in a segregated facility and pays below minimum wage.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: A person 'on a waiver' gets home and community-based services paid for through one of the waiver programs listed above.

How likely one group is to have an outcome, compared with everyone else. 1.0 means no difference. Below 1 means less likely. Above 1 means more likely. Example: 0.5 means half as likely; 2.0 means twice as likely.
terms.source: FY22_24 Equity Data, Info and Key

terms.plain: A person whose case-mix classification shows they need more support.

terms.full: People on a waiver served at home
terms.plain: A person on a waiver who did not use a residential service (such as a group home) that year.
Working-age people on a disability waiver who had income from wages or self-employment.
National standards for respectful, understandable services for people of every culture and language.
An assessment of how a person approaches cultural difference.
terms.source: ADSA Equity and Inclusion Implementation Plan
